reviews_5s:
Alright, fellow sourdough parents and anyone who appreciates beautiful glass containers, let me tell you about my recent upgrade: the Weck Tulip Jars (1 Liter, set of 4). For a while, my sourdough starter, lovingly named "Bubbles," lived in a less-than-glamorous repurposed jar. It was functional, sure, but it lacked... panache. Bubbles deserved better. I deserved a more aesthetically pleasing fermentation station.

I saw these Weck jars online and was immediately smitten. The tulip shape is adorable, the glass looks thick and sturdy, and those little glass lids with the rubber seals and metal clips? So classic! They look like they belong in a European pantry straight out of a fairytale. My plastic containers felt a pang of jealousy.

When these arrived, they felt just as good as they looked. Solid, heavy glass. The wide mouth is fantastic for feeding Bubbles (less mess!) and for cleaning (my whole hand actually fits inside!). The separate lid, rubber gasket, and clips are easy to assemble and provide a satisfyingly airtight seal. It's like giving your contents a little glass vault.

Bubbles took to its new home immediately. It seems happier, more active, and frankly, more sophisticated. The clear glass lets me easily monitor its bubbling progress, which is both fascinating and slightly hypnotic. I've also used these jars for storing other things – leftover soup, overnight oats, even just displaying colorful dried beans. They make everything look instantly more organized and charming. It's like my pantry got a mini-makeover.

The versatility is a huge plus. Canning, storage, fermentation, or just looking pretty on a shelf – these jars can do it all. They're dishwasher safe (hallelujah!), and the thick glass makes them feel incredibly durable. I feel confident that these will be housing future generations of sourdough starters (and maybe even some actual canned goods, if I ever get that ambitious).

If you're a sourdough enthusiast, appreciate high-quality glass containers, or just want to bring a touch of classic European charm and organization to your kitchen, these Weck Tulip Jars are a fantastic choice. They're beautiful, practical, and have made my fermentation station (and my pantry) significantly more delightful. I'm thoroughly impressed with these charming jars.I bought this set of two Weck jars to use for my sourdough starter. Each week, I take out 50-75 grams of starter to feed in one jar, marked with a green rubberband to indicate the starting level, and use for my next loaf of bread. I put the discard in the other jar (with a purple rubber band around it to mark the level) to use in biscuits, waffles, English muffins, etc throughout the week. It’s a great system to keep my sourdough well-fed and maintained.

The jars have nice, wide mouths, which makes it easy to get the starter in and out. They’re thick, sturdy glass that won’t break if you bump them into something or tap a spoon against the edge. I use the glass lid and rubber gasket without the clips, so the gasses released by my starter don’t build up pressure inside the jar.

It is exactly what I needed, and I’m glad I went with this option, rather than some of the plastic options I saw labeled as sourdough starter jars. Both jars (my active and my discard) live on the top shelf in my refrigerator, since I usually don’t bake bread more than once a week, and don’t want to have to feed/discard every day. I usually feed Friday evening and leave the active jar out overnight to double, then bake with it on Saturday.These are best soug dough starter jars because have wide mouth and main point THERE ARE NO RIDGES AT TOP. Mason jars have ridges and its hard to clean all ridges at top. This jar easy to keep clean and versatile with lid on when starter is on counter then using seals and clips when starter needs to stay air tight in refrigerator. Plus its cute jar set on counter too. These jars are thicker heavyweight glass too making them best all around glass jar.I got these for my mom who has been really getting into sourdough. They are very big (larger than the typical mason jar by maybe 20%) and perfect for feeding a new starter/adding more flour. As any sourdough-maker knows, you can't mix starters without compromising the original yeast, so coming in a two pack means they are useful for more than one strain of yeast. They are also sturdy and great quality for the price. Would purchase again.I love these jars! They are great for sourdough starter and all other things! I use them all the time. Lids fit well, great shape and I love the tint too!It is as described. I’m using for my sourdough starter. I like the wide mouth glass jar.These are perfect for sourdough starter.These Wek jars work wonders for sour dough starters!Best jars I've used for my sourdough starter. They are easy to mix in, store the starter or discard in, easy to wipe the residue out (so it doesn't clog up your water pipes!), and pretty to boot!If you are a home baker making two loaves at a time these are the PERFECT size, no need for those huge 'starter jars'. The glass is nice and thick,(unlike my 'starter jars' that were so thin that I broke one bumping it in my stainless sink).
My tulip jars arrived with no damage or chips in the rims. The rounded side to bottom transition makes the stirring and scrape-down super easy and they are not so tall ...so now my stirring implement isn't too short.

reviews_1s:
I had high hopes for these jar, intending to use them for my homemade vegan milk, yogurts and kefir. I've been using Mason jars, which have a narrower neck than body, making it hard to get all the food out of them. As a result I've been wasting a little of food in each jar.

I bought these Weck jars because they don't have a narrow neck, they look like I can spatula out pretty much every drop of my yogurt, etc. fairly easily.

The problem is the lids. I got some that are defective, the rubber is stretched too loose to fit the jar. Even if the rubber gasket fit, it just lies on the top of the rim, it doesn't stay in any groove in the lid, so takes a really fiddly few minutes to open and close these jars.

I expected the clamps to be a little fidgety, so I bought this set that comes with the white snap on lids. My lids were misshapen, and they're made of a really cheap plastic. The clamps are made of thin, cheap metal, too. I doubt either those lids or clamps would last.

I would not have kept this set even if it weren't defective. Don't blame manufacturers ONLY SELLER!!!!!Received a crack one, probably rainforest issueGosh, they're nice jars and tops, but the clips and seal are bad design.
First, the two clips/clamps that hold the lid on aren't permanently/solidly attached, so as soon as you take them off, they become two loose pieces that you need to try and not lose. And the rubber seal, makes a good seal, but you kinda need to hold it on with both hands while reattaching the lid.
I was going to use this for daily sourdough discard (good size bottle) but between the clips and seal hassle, I'm not sure it's worth the daily issue.
If you were using these to seal something for a long period of limited access, I'm sure it'd be fine. But for quick/repeated on/off . . . this might be more trouble than it's worth.Hate the clips, they fling off.
